- When sentiment is negative and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If recent price history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive downward moves), model should not over-forecast rebound.  
- Overshoots after sharp spikes (e.g., +15%+ above recent peak) should be capped at +10% of prior peak to avoid over-leverage.  
- If sentiment is positive but forecast is flat or declining, increase forecast by 3–7% to capture sentiment-driven momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% in 2+ consecutive days, adjust next forecast downward by 2–5% to avoid momentum trap.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ negative sentiment days in row), forecast should be 3–5% below historical mean of recent 7-day window.
